questions.stem: Based on this image, which of the following statements are true? (Choose three.)

options.text: Attributes from two tables populate a table with the same name as a ServiceNow CMDB table.
This operation is more than likely a part of a step on a pattern set to Application Pattern Type.
If a value is unmatched, it is still merged into the Target Table.
For this operation to run, there must be some data in the process.executablePath variable.
This is a horizontal pattern of type "infrastructure."

questions.explanation: The image shows a Merge Table operation with Target Table=$cmdb_ci_web_server, which matches a CMDB table name (A). The $process.executablePath variable is used in the merge criteria condition, which is specific to Application patterns — infrastructure patterns don't use executablePath (B is true, E is false). This variable must contain data for the condition to evaluate and the operation to run (D). Unmatched Values is set to 'Remove', meaning unmatched values are NOT merged into the target table, so C is false.

questions.stem: Based on the following images, which choice best describes what occurs if Discovery sets the name attribute of a discovered Windows Server CI to 'Windows1' and then Altiris discovery runs detecting 'Windows2' for the name attribute on the same CI?

options.text: The name of the CI stays 'Windows1'.
The name of the CI changes to 'Windows2'.
The name of the CI does not populate with either discovery.
The CI is not discovered because Discovery is not listed in either image.

questions.explanation: The image shows Data Source Precedences: ServiceNow order=100 (highest priority), OpenView=200, Altiris=300 (lowest priority). Lower order number means higher precedence. When Discovery (ServiceNow, order 100) sets name='Windows1' first, Altiris (order 300) cannot overwrite it because Altiris has lower precedence. A higher-precedence source's data is protected from being overwritten by a lower-precedence source. The name stays 'Windows1' (A).

questions.stem: For the Parse Variable pattern operation, what is required to have two different parsing methods to populate variables?

options.text: A tabular and a scalar variable.
Two different Define Parsing selections on the same step.

questions.explanation: To use two different parsing methods in a Parse Variable operation, you need two different steps. Each Parse Variable operation supports only one parsing strategy (e.g., Delimited Text or Regular Expression) per step. To apply two different parsing methods to populate variables, you must create two separate steps with different Define Parsing configurations.

questions.stem: Which best describes Discovery schedule of type Configuration Item?

options.text: Verifies Configuration Item data from the scanned IP ranges against the data in the CMDB.
Creates only a list of discovered IPs in both IPv4 and IPv6 formats.
Collects complete information from the scanned IP ranges and sends it to the CMDB.
Directly populates records in the assets table.

questions.explanation: A Discovery schedule of type Configuration Item collects complete information from the scanned IP ranges and sends it to the CMDB. Unlike IP Discovery (which only creates a list of IPs), CI Discovery performs full exploration including hardware, software, and relationships. It does not simply verify data against the CMDB or populate the assets table directly.

questions.stem: When installing a MID Server on a Windows platform, which right must be associated when creating a Service Account?
questions.explanation: When installing a MID Server on Windows, the service account must have the 'Log on as a service' right. The MID Server runs as a Windows service, so this permission is required for the service account to start and operate correctly. Root is a Linux concept, Domain Admin is excessive, and MID Server User Role is a ServiceNow platform role, not a Windows right.

questions.stem: Which of the below choices are needed for Quick Discovery? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Quick Discovery requires a MID Server (to execute the discovery probes) and a Target IP (the specific IP address to discover). Quick Discovery is a simplified way to discover a single device without creating a full Discovery Schedule. A Discovery Schedule and PID are not needed for Quick Discovery.

questions.stem: In order to use Debug from the Pattern Designer, you must have what?
questions.explanation: To use Debug from the Pattern Designer, you must have a discoverable CI — an actual device or system that the pattern can be tested against in debug mode. Debug mode connects to a real target to execute pattern steps. A proxy server, admin role, and Service Mapping are not prerequisites for pattern debugging.

questions.stem:
A discovery runs against a Windows Server returning the following attribute values for the first time: name = WindowsSN1 serial_number = 12321
A subsequent discovery runs against a different Windows Server returning the following attribute values: name = WindowsSN2 serial_number = 12321
With only base system CI Identifiers configured, which of the following is true?

options.text: A Windows Server CI is created, then updated with WindowsSN2 as the name.
Two Windows Sewer CIs are created, with WindowsSN1 AND WindowsSN2 for names.
Two Windows Server CIs are created, without serial_number values.
A Windows Server CI is created, then updated with WindowsSN1 as the name.

questions.explanation: With base system CI Identifiers, Windows Servers are identified by serial_number. The first discovery creates a CI with name='WindowsSN1' and serial_number='12321'. The second discovery finds a device with serial_number='12321' — the IRE matches it to the existing CI and updates the name to 'WindowsSN2'. Same serial number means same CI, so the name gets updated.

questions.stem: Which choice represents the three best ways of extending Discovery?
questions.explanation: The three best ways of extending Discovery are Classifiers (for identifying new CI types), Probes and Sensors (for collecting custom data via the ECC Queue), and Discovery Patterns (for defining custom discovery logic). Orchestration and Fingerprinting are separate features not considered primary Discovery extension methods.

questions.stem: SNMP Credentials require which of the following?
questions.explanation: SNMP credentials require read community strings for Discovery. SNMP v1/v2c uses community strings for authentication, and Discovery only needs read access to query device information. Write community strings are not needed for discovery (read-only operation). Usernames are used in SNMP v3, and port 135 is for Windows RPC, not SNMP.

questions.stem: Which choice will populate the Location field for a discovered CI?

options.text: Location field for a Discovery Schedule
Location field for a parent CI Type
Location field for a Port Probe
Location report from the Discovery Dashboard

questions.explanation: The Location field for a discovered CI is populated from the Location field defined on the Discovery Schedule. When a schedule runs, all CIs discovered through that schedule inherit the location specified on the schedule. CI Type, Port Probe, and Discovery Dashboard location reports do not populate CI location fields.

questions.stem: What role is needed by the MID Server's user account to interact with a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: The MID Server's user account requires the mid_server role to interact with a ServiceNow instance. This role grants the necessary permissions for the MID Server to read probe instructions from and write sensor results to the ECC Queue. The discovery_admin and sm_mid roles serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Which operation is used to change from the default credentials to any other appropriate credentials in a horizontal pattern?
questions.explanation: The Alternate credentials operation is used to change from default credentials to other appropriate credentials in a horizontal pattern. When the initial credentials don't work for a specific target, this operation allows the pattern to try alternative credential sets. Change credentials, Change user, and Alternate user are not valid pattern operation names.

questions.stem: After navigating to an Automaton Error Messages list from Discovery > Home, how are the options on the right navigation pane categorized? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Automaton Error Messages list's right navigation pane is categorized into SELECT ONE (to choose a specific error type or action) and ACTION ON ALL (to perform bulk actions on all error messages). These two categories organize how users interact with discovery error recommendations.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used in the Debug Identification Section in Debug Mode for an infrastructure pattern? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: In Debug Mode for an infrastructure pattern, the Debug Identification Section accepts IP address and Host Name as identification parameters. These are the standard network identifiers used to locate and connect to infrastructure devices. AWS Endpoint is for cloud patterns, and PID (Process ID) is for application patterns.

questions.stem: With multiple CI data sources, which choice is the best for determining which source can update a CI attribute?
questions.explanation: Reconciliation Rules are the best mechanism for determining which data source can update a CI attribute when multiple sources exist. Reconciliation rules define data source precedence, specifying which source takes priority for each attribute. Business Rules are general-purpose, Transform Maps handle imports, and Data Certification is for data quality.

questions.stem: One method for deleting specific CIs not discovered in 30 days is:
questions.explanation: A Scheduled Job can be configured to delete or mark CIs that haven't been discovered within a specified period (e.g., 30 days). This automates the cleanup of stale CIs. UI Policies control form behavior, Service Mapping discovers services, and Data Policies enforce field requirements — none handle time-based CI deletion.

questions.stem: Which of the following choices must be installed on a MID Server to run Credential-less Discovery?
questions.explanation: Nmap must be installed on the MID Server host to run Credential-less Discovery. Nmap enables network scanning and OS fingerprinting without requiring login credentials on target devices. Credential-less Extension, Advanced IP Scanner, and Defender are not components used for credential-less discovery in ServiceNow.

questions.stem:
A network device has both an SSH port and an SNMP port open. Discovery tries the SSH probe first and it fails. This triggers the SNMP probe, which succeeds. Discovery uses SNMP first for subsequent discoveries on that device.
What discovery functionality allows the above to happen?
questions.explanation: Credential affinity allows Discovery to remember which credentials (and their associated protocol) successfully connected to a device. After SSH fails and SNMP succeeds, credential affinity records the working SNMP credential for that IP. On subsequent discoveries, the system tries the SNMP credential first, avoiding the failed SSH attempt.

questions.stem: The CMDB contains which of the following record types? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The CMDB contains Configuration Items (CIs) and Relation Types as its core record types. CIs represent managed entities (servers, applications, etc.), and Relation Types (cmdb_rel_type) define the relationships between CIs. Models and Assets are IT Asset Management (ITAM) records stored in separate tables outside the core CMDB.

questions.stem: When is the Extension section in a horizontal pattern executed?

options.text: As part of the post sensor processing script
As part of the port scan

questions.explanation: The Extension section in a horizontal pattern is executed after the Identification sections complete. Extensions run additional discovery logic after the main CI has been identified. They are not part of port scanning, post-sensor processing, or executed before identification.

questions.stem: For CMDB Health, relationships can be which of the following choices? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: For CMDB Health, relationships can be categorized as Stale (not updated within expected timeframe), Required (mandatory relationships that should exist), and Recommended (suggested relationships for completeness). These three categories are used in the Compliance KPI. Duplicate and Orphan are CI-level health metrics, not relationship types.

questions.stem: Which of the choices provides active discovery errors with a help link for each error?
questions.explanation: The Discovery Dashboard provides active discovery errors with a help link for each error. The dashboard shows error summaries with links to troubleshooting guidance. The IP Address Failure Report shows failed IPs, Discovery Schedule shows configuration, and MID Server Dashboard shows MID Server health — none provide error-specific help links.

questions.stem: What related list on a classifier dictates which Horizontal Pattern probe is launched?
questions.explanation: The Triggers probes related list on a classifier dictates which Horizontal Pattern probe is launched when a device matches the classifier. This related list maps classification matches to specific pattern probes for execution. Discovery Log, Classification Criteria, and Pattern probes are not the related list that controls probe triggering.

questions.stem: Which of the following does the ECC Queue provide? (Choose two.)

options.text: Login credentials for the MID Server host.
The actual XML payload that is sent to or from an instance.
A connected flow of probe and sensor activity.
The process responsible for defining, analyzing, planning, measuring, and improving all aspects of the availability of IT services.

questions.explanation: The ECC Queue provides the actual XML payload sent to or from an instance (the raw data exchanged between the instance and MID Server) and a connected flow of probe and sensor activity (showing the sequence of discovery operations). It does not store MID Server login credentials or provide ITIL process definitions.

questions.stem: Which of the following choices are only used for the Application Pattern Type? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Run Order and Operating System are fields only used for Application Pattern Type patterns. Run Order determines execution sequence among multiple application patterns, and Operating System specifies which OS the pattern applies to. CI Type and Identification Section are used in both infrastructure and application patterns.

questions.stem: By default, which of the following are automatically available as variables for horizontal discovery patterns? (Choose two.)

options.text: The CI Type on the Discovery Pattern form

questions.explanation: For horizontal discovery patterns, the CI Type specified on the Discovery Pattern form and the computer_system variable are automatically available as default variables. The CI Type becomes a variable representing the target CI class, and computer_system represents the discovered computer. infrastructure_system and windows_cmdb_ci are not default automatic variables.

questions.stem: Which choices are necessary to launch any pattern? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: To launch any Discovery pattern, two pieces of information are required: CI Classification and CI Type. CI Classification determines the device category (e.g., Computer, Network Gear) based on open ports and protocol responses. CI Type refines this to a specific OS or device type (e.g., Linux, Windows, Cisco IOS). Together they select which pattern to execute. CI Serial Number is an output of discovery, not a prerequisite. Data Certification is a CMDB governance concept unrelated to pattern launch.

questions.stem: Which of the below choices are horizontal pattern types? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two horizontal pattern types are Infrastructure (for discovering OS, hardware, and network devices) and Application (for discovering software applications running on CIs). Hardware and Software are CI categories or discovery phases, not pattern types. Horizontal patterns are always classified as either Infrastructure or Application.

questions.stem: What does the MID Server need to collect vCenter events?
questions.explanation: The MID Server needs the vCenter Event Collector extension to collect vCenter events. This extension enables the MID Server to monitor and relay VMware vCenter event data to the ServiceNow instance. SNMP Trap Listener is for SNMP events, firewalls block traffic, and vCenter probes are used for standard discovery, not event collection.

questions.stem:
A Discovery Schedule contains a /24 subnet IP Range and a Shazzam batch size of 5000.
How many times will a Shazzam probe be launched during discovery?
questions.explanation: A /24 subnet contains 254 usable IP addresses. With a Shazzam batch size of 5000, all 254 IPs fit within a single batch. Therefore, only 1 Shazzam probe is launched. The batch size exceeds the total number of IPs, so no splitting is needed. If the subnet had more than 5000 IPs, multiple probes would be created.

questions.stem: Which method is used by Discovery to determine if a Host IP is active or alive?
questions.explanation: Discovery uses a Port Scan (via the Shazzam probe) to determine if a host IP is active or alive. Shazzam sends TCP/UDP packets to common ports and checks for responses. If any port responds, the IP is considered active. Ping (ICMP) is not used by default, Traceroute maps network paths, and Classification happens after the host is confirmed active.

questions.stem: Discovery finds and maps dependencies for the following types of storage devices. (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Discovery finds and maps dependencies for three types of storage devices: Direct-attached storage (DAS), Network-attached storage (NAS), and Storage area network (SAN). These represent the major enterprise storage architectures. MAN (Multiple area network) is a networking term, and RAID is a disk redundancy technology, not a storage device type Discovery maps.

questions.stem:
Which choice allows the following functionality to occur?
If this value is set to 1000 and a discovery must scan 10,000 IP addresses using a single MID Server, it creates 10 Shazzam probes with each probe scanning 1000 IP addresses.
questions.explanation: Shazzam Batch Size controls how many IP addresses each Shazzam probe scans. When set to 1000 with 10,000 IPs to scan, it creates 10 separate Shazzam probes each scanning 1000 addresses. This distributes the scanning workload. MID Server Clusters, selection methods, and Behaviors serve different purposes in Discovery.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes how to use a Behavior for discovery?

options.text: The MID Server selection method on a Discovery Schedule.
The Behavior drop-down menu on a Discovery IP Range.
The Behavior drop-down menu on a Discovery Status.
The Behavior checkbox on a CI.

questions.explanation: A Behavior is applied through the Behavior drop-down menu on a Discovery IP Range. Behaviors define how Discovery interacts with devices in that IP range (e.g., which protocols to use, timeout settings). They are configured per IP range, not on schedules, statuses, or individual CIs.

questions.stem: Which of the following pattern operations query targets? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: WMI Query and Get Process are pattern operations that query targets — they connect to the target device and retrieve information. WMI Query executes WMI queries on Windows targets, and Get Process retrieves running process information. Merge Table operates on local data, and Parse Variable processes existing variable content without querying the target.

questions.stem: File-based Discovery is triggered during the __________.
questions.explanation: File-based Discovery is triggered during the Exploration Phase. After a device is classified and identified, the Exploration phase collects detailed information including file contents. File-based discovery reads configuration files during this phase. The Scan phase finds IPs, Classification identifies device types, and Identification determines CI identity.

questions.stem: Given a custom column named u_custom_column on table cmdb_ci_linux_server, which variable syntax should be used to populate the column in a horizontal discovery pattern using the Set Parameter Value operation?
questions.explanation: The correct variable syntax for a custom column u_custom_column on table cmdb_ci_linux_server is $cmdb_ci_linux_server[*].u_custom_column. This syntax specifies the table name, [*] to indicate all rows/instances, and the column name after the dot. The Set Parameter Value operation uses this format to populate CI attributes.

questions.stem: What entry point type must a horizontal pattern have to execute from a process classifier?

options.text: HTTP(S) entry point type if the pattern is running on a web server application.
TCP entry point type or ALL entry point type.
It does not matter, it is triggered for all entry point types.

questions.explanation: A horizontal pattern must have a TCP entry point type or ALL entry point type to execute from a process classifier. Process classifiers detect running processes on TCP ports, so the pattern must accept TCP connections as entry points. The ALL entry point type includes TCP. HTTP(S) and subnet entry points serve different triggering mechanisms.

questions.stem: Which metrics comprise the Completeness KPI for CMDB Health? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Completeness KPI for CMDB Health is comprised of two metrics: Required (mandatory attributes that must be populated) and Recommended (suggested attributes that should be populated). Completeness measures how thoroughly CI records are filled in across these two categories. Audit and Overall are not Completeness sub-metrics.

questions.stem: Which of the following choices explain differences between Service Mapping and Discovery? (Choose two.)

options.text: Discovery requires agent installation to find hardware devices, Service Mapping requires agents for software.
Discovery finds applications and devices on your network, Service Mapping monitors those devices.
Discovery utilizes IP address ranges for initial discovery, Service Mapping uses entry points.
Discovery addresses inventory-related use-cases, while Service Mapping allows for the creation of accurate maps of application service topologies.

questions.explanation: Two key differences between Service Mapping and Discovery: Discovery utilizes IP address ranges for initial scanning while Service Mapping uses entry points (C), and Discovery addresses inventory/CMDB use-cases while Service Mapping creates accurate application service topology maps (D). Neither requires agents, and Service Mapping does not monitor devices.

questions.stem: What are the two main options within a Parse File operation?
questions.explanation: The two main options within a Parse File operation are Select File (choose which file to parse from the target) and Define Parsing (specify the parsing strategy — delimited text, regex, etc.). These two selections configure what file to read and how to extract data from it. The other options describe unrelated Discovery features.

questions.stem: Based on the following image, which of the following choices is also true about London Linux Servers?

options.text: It is a CMDB Group with Dashboard Group type.
It is a CMDB Group with Health Group type.
It is a Datacenter Group in London.
It is a CMDB Group with Default Group type.

questions.explanation: Based on the image context showing London Linux Servers, this is a CMDB Group with Health Group type. CMDB Health groups are created to monitor the health of specific CI collections. Health Group type allows the group to appear in CMDB Health dashboards for monitoring completeness, compliance, and correctness of the grouped CIs.

questions.stem: For the Set Parameter Value operation, which of the following is used in the syntax to declare a constant, unchanging Value?
questions.explanation: In the Set Parameter Value operation, quotes are used to declare a constant, unchanging value. When a value is enclosed in quotes, it is treated as a literal string rather than a variable reference. Dollar signs ($) reference variables, brackets reference array elements, and hash tags are not used for constants.

questions.stem: From an SNMP Query pattern operation, which of the choices are valid Variable Types? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: From an SNMP Query pattern operation, the valid Variable Types are Table (for SNMP tables returning multiple rows of data) and Scalar (for single-value SNMP objects). SNMP MIBs define objects as either scalar (single value) or tabular (multiple rows). Test and CI Type are not SNMP variable types.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes what happens when, by default, duplicate CIs are detected during identification and reconciliation?

options.text: A notification is sent to the CI owner.
An associated identification rule is created automatically.
Each set of duplicate CIs is added to a de-duplication task.
The next discovery is stopped for the CI that is duplicated.

questions.explanation: By default, when duplicate CIs are detected during identification and reconciliation, each set of duplicate CIs is added to a de-duplication task. These tasks appear in the CMDB Health dashboard for administrators to review and resolve. No automatic notification, identification rule creation, or discovery stopping occurs by default.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes a horizontal discovery pattern?
questions.explanation: A horizontal discovery pattern is best described as steps that execute operations. Patterns consist of ordered steps, where each step contains one or more operations (WMI Query, Parse Variable, Set Parameter Value, etc.) that collect and process discovery data. Patterns are not credential depots, port scanning tools, or classifiers.

questions.stem:
A config file for an application has the following three lines:
Line 1: app build 1.2.3.4 version 5.14
Line 2: installation_dir=c:\opt\bin
Line 3: build_type=Server.
Which methods below will extract the build and version numbers from these lines using a horizontal discovery pattern? (Choose two.)

options.text: Get Process operation with correct Port
Find Matching URL operation with Target Variable
Parse File operation with Delimited Text parsing strategy
Parse File operation with Regular Expression parsing strategy

questions.explanation: To extract build and version numbers from the config file, two Parse File methods work: Delimited Text parsing (using space or = as delimiters to extract fields from lines) and Regular Expression parsing (using regex patterns to capture specific build/version number formats). Get Process and Find Matching URL are unrelated to file content extraction.

questions.stem:
The following shows part of the Windows OS - Servers pattern in Pattern Designer:

Which of the steps above use(s) a shared library?
questions.explanation: The image shows two steps in Pattern Designer: Step 25 'Windows - Storage' has the shared library icon (stacked list indicator), while Step 26 'Insert total disk space of the server' has a regular step icon (single document). In Pattern Designer, shared libraries are reusable step collections indicated by a distinct list icon. Only Step 25 uses a shared library (C). Step 26 is a standalone step.

questions.stem: Which of the following is required for a MID Server to have access to automatically stay up-to-date with instance versions?
questions.explanation: The MID Server needs access to install.service-now.com to automatically stay up-to-date with instance versions. This URL hosts the MID Server update packages that allow automatic version synchronization. The docs, developer, and main service-now.com sites do not provide MID Server auto-update packages.

questions.stem: When designing steps with operations requiring variables, it is best practice to do what?
questions.explanation: When designing steps with operations requiring variables, best practice is to query targets for variables rather than hardcoding values. Querying targets ensures the pattern gets current, accurate data from the actual device. Hardcoding variables, using only scalar types, and designing for static environments create brittle patterns that break when environments change.

questions.stem: For what is File Based Discovery used?

options.text: To discover the checksum of a file and store it to track for changes
To discover the contents of flat files such as configuration files
To discover that file names conform to a defined naming standard
To discover file paths to recognize the signature of installed software

questions.explanation: File Based Discovery is used to discover file paths to recognize the signature of installed software. It scans for specific file paths and patterns that identify software installations on target systems, matching them against known software signatures in the Software Library. It does not check file checksums, read file contents, or validate naming standards.

questions.stem: Which of the following properties define the maximum overall size for the returned payload that comes from patterns?
questions.explanation: The property mid.discovery.max_pattern_payload_size defines the maximum overall size for returned payloads from patterns. This property controls how much data a pattern can send back from the MID Server to the instance. The other property names are not valid ServiceNow Discovery properties.

questions.stem: Based on this image, which of the following choices is true?

options.text: This is from a WMI query operation step.
There is a scalar variable labeled ‘1’.
This Value cannot be used in a pattern step.
There is a tabular variable named ‘name_details’.

questions.explanation: Based on the image context, the result shows a tabular variable named 'name_details' containing multiple rows of data returned from a query operation. Tabular variables store multi-row results where each row has named columns. The image does not show a WMI query step specifically, nor a scalar variable labeled '1'.

questions.stem: Using the SNMP Query operation on a pattern for a custom device query, it is best practice to do what?

options.text: Enable SSH as a secondary protocol
Use the publish manufacturer’s device MIB

questions.explanation: When using the SNMP Query operation for a custom device, best practice is to use the published manufacturer's device MIB. The manufacturer's MIB contains the correct OIDs and data types for the specific device, ensuring accurate discovery. Modifying default MIBs, enabling SSH, and using live production devices are all against best practices.

questions.stem: After running Discovery and viewing the ECC Queue tab, what are some of the displayed default fields? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The ECC Queue tab displays several default fields including Topic (what the probe/sensor is about), Queue (Input or Output direction), and Source (where the message originated). These are core ECC Queue fields visible by default. Details, CMDB CI, Pattern log link, and Discovery schedule name are not default ECC fields.

questions.stem:
Hardware Models can have a one-to-many relationship with the following:
(Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Hardware Models can have a one-to-many relationship with Assets (many assets can reference one model), Configuration Items (many CIs can reference one model), and Model Categories (through the model category hierarchy). Manufacturer and Product owner are typically many-to-one relationships from the model perspective.

questions.stem: Which choice best represents how to modify the functionality shown in this image?
questions.explanation: Based on the image context, the functionality shown is modified from a Classifier. Classifiers determine how discovered devices are categorized and which probes or patterns are triggered. Modifying classifier criteria, match rules, or triggered probes changes Discovery behavior for device classification.

questions.stem: What is the recommended method of consolidating duplicate CIs?
questions.explanation: The Duplicate CI Remediator is the recommended method for consolidating duplicate CIs in ServiceNow. It provides a structured workflow for reviewing and merging duplicate CI records identified by the IRE. Manual remediation is error-prone, Event CI Remediation handles events, and Ignore Duplicate CI just suppresses the issue without resolving it.

questions.stem: During the Discovery process, what determines if an Asset record is created?
questions.explanation: During Discovery, the Model Category determines if an Asset record is created for a discovered CI. If the model category associated with the CI's hardware model is configured for asset tracking, an asset record is automatically generated. The CMDB, ECC Queue, Model Product, and CI record itself do not control asset creation.

questions.stem: What pattern operation allows the transfer of a file from the MID Server to a target?
questions.explanation: The Put File operation transfers a file from the MID Server to a target device. This is useful for deploying configuration files or scripts to discovered systems. Parse File reads files from targets, Create Connection establishes connectivity, and Manage Attachments handles ServiceNow record attachments — none transfer files to targets.

questions.stem: On the ECC Queue, sensor records have a Queue value of ___________ and probe records have a Queue value of ___________.
questions.explanation: On the ECC Queue, sensor records have a Queue value of 'input' (data coming IN from MID Server with results) and probe records have a Queue value of 'output' (commands going OUT to the MID Server for execution). This input/output naming reflects the direction relative to the ServiceNow instance.

questions.stem: In Discovery, what table associates an IP address and a credential?
questions.explanation: The Credential Affinity table (dscy_credentials_affinity) associates an IP address with a credential in Discovery. When a credential successfully authenticates against a device, the affinity is recorded so Discovery can use the same credential first on subsequent runs. Service Affinity, Service CI Association, and Tags serve different purposes.

questions.stem: If the WMI service is not running on a host, it will prevent the discovery of which devices?
questions.explanation: WMI (Windows Management Instrumentation) is a Windows-specific management technology used by Discovery to query Windows devices for hardware, software, and configuration details. If the WMI service is not running on a host, Discovery cannot gather information from that Windows machine. WMI is irrelevant to Network devices (which use SNMP), Unix/Linux devices (which use SSH), and Storage devices (which use SMI-S or vendor APIs). Only Windows devices depend on WMI for Discovery.

questions.stem: In general, Discovery can provide which of the following kinds of application relationships? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Discovery can provide application-to-application relationships (connections between software applications) and host-to-application relationships (which applications run on which hosts). These are the two main relationship types Discovery creates for applications. TCP-to-UDP is a protocol concept, and MID server-to-target is an infrastructure relationship not stored in CMDB.

questions.stem: Which of the following must be configured to allow a MID Server to access servers using WinRM? (Choose two.)

options.text: MID Servers must be configured as a trusted source with DNS
MID Servers need to be added to the WinRM Group policy on the Servers

questions.explanation: To allow MID Server access via WinRM, two configurations are needed: MID Servers need to be added to the WinRM Group Policy on target servers (allowing WinRM connections from the MID Server IP) and MID Server Parameters must include WinRM configuration. JEA is optional, and DNS trusted source configuration is not a WinRM requirement.

questions.stem:
For a pattern operation, which of the below choices could be a valid replacement for <_>? (Choose three.)
$IfTable<_>.InstanceID
questions.explanation: In the pattern variable syntax $IfTable<_>.InstanceID, valid replacements for <_> include [3] (specific row index), [*] (wildcard matching all rows), and [] (empty brackets for current element). [X] is not a valid index, [&] is not a recognized operator, and [.] is not valid syntax for table row reference.

questions.stem: Which of the below choices are the most probable results of the following image? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Based on the image showing a WMI Query operation for Win32_Process, the most probable results are three scalar variables: MaximumWorkingSetSize, PageFaults, and PeakVirtualSize. These are individual process metrics returned as scalar values from the WMI query. The query name itself is not a variable, and the result set naming follows the field names.

questions.stem: What is found on the far-right section of the Pattern Designer for horizontal patterns? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The far-right section of the Pattern Designer for horizontal patterns displays CI Attributes (showing available CMDB fields for the CI type) and Temporary Variables (showing variables defined within the pattern). These two panels help pattern designers map discovered data to CI fields. Operations are in the center panel, and CMDB Dashboard is a separate interface.

questions.stem: Which of the choices below best represent key capabilities of a ServiceNow ITOM Enterprise solution? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Key capabilities of a ServiceNow ITOM Enterprise solution include Manage Hybrid Clouds (cloud management and governance) and Proactively Eliminate Service Outages (AIOps, event management, health monitoring). Creating engaging user experiences and building apps fast are platform/development capabilities, not ITOM-specific.

questions.stem: Which choices best describe what is necessary to create a custom horizontal pattern to discover an operating system that is not discovered by the base installation patterns? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: To create a custom horizontal pattern for discovering a new operating system, you must select a CI Type (the CMDB class for the OS) and select Infrastructure Pattern Type (OS discovery uses infrastructure patterns, not application patterns). Application pattern type is for software, and process strategy is not a required selection.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the Tomcat [cmdb_ci_app_server_tomcat] table and the Application Server [cdmb_ci_app_server] table? (Choose two.)

options.text: Tomcat does not extend the Application Server table
Tomcat table extends the Application Server table
Tomcat table is a child of the Application Server table
Tomcat table is a parent of the Application Server table

questions.explanation: The Tomcat table (cmdb_ci_app_server_tomcat) extends the Application Server table (cmdb_ci_app_server) and is therefore a child of the Application Server table. In ServiceNow's table hierarchy, extending a table creates a parent-child relationship where the child inherits all fields from the parent. Tomcat is not a parent of Application Server.

questions.stem: In a discovery pattern, which types are available with CI Attributes in the Pattern Designer? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: In the Pattern Designer, CI Attributes are available for the Main pattern CI type (the primary CI being discovered) and Related CI types (CIs that have relationships with the main CI). Global CI types and All CI types are not specific categories available in the Pattern Designer's CI Attributes section.

questions.stem: Which of the below choices are benefits of Tracked Configuration Files? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Benefits of Tracked Configuration Files include content version comparison (ability to compare different versions of configuration files over time) and files tracked as CIs (configuration files are stored as CI records in the CMDB). Tracked files do not remove unwanted files from targets, and credentials are still needed for file access.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes a Functionality Definition?

options.text: Defines what CI identifiers to use.
Defines the IP addresses to discover.
Defines what Behavior to use from a Discovery Schedule.
Defines what protocols to detect from within a Behavior.

questions.explanation: A Functionality Definition defines what protocols to detect from within a Behavior. Functionality definitions specify which network services (SSH, SNMP, WMI, etc.) a Discovery Behavior should look for when scanning devices. They do not define CI identifiers, IP addresses for discovery, or which Behavior to use on a schedule.

questions.stem: As a first step in horizontal discovery, which of the following is where the Shazzam probe is placed in a request?
questions.explanation: As the first step in horizontal discovery, the Shazzam probe is placed in a request on the ECC Queue. The ECC Queue is the communication channel between the ServiceNow instance and MID Server. All probes, including Shazzam, are sent to the MID Server via the ECC Queue's Output queue for execution.

questions.stem: Which of the choices have a higher chance of leading to lost data during CI reclassification? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: During CI reclassification, Switching (moving to a different CI class at the same hierarchy level) and Downgrading (moving to a parent/higher-level class) have a higher chance of leading to lost data. Both operations can result in losing class-specific attributes that don't exist in the target class. Upgrading preserves data, and Identifying is not a reclassification action.

questions.stem: Which of the below choices are kinds of variables used in discovery patterns? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three kinds of variables used in discovery patterns are CI attributes (values that map to CMDB fields), Temporary variables (local variables used within the pattern for intermediate calculations), and Global variables (variables available across all steps like computer_system). Prefix and Fixed are not variable kinds in discovery patterns.

questions.stem: Which of the following choices may be global variables for steps in horizontal discovery patterns? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: For horizontal discovery patterns, computer_system and process are global variables available to steps. The computer_system variable represents the discovered host CI (available in infrastructure patterns), and the process variable represents the application process (available in application patterns). System and baseline are not standard global pattern variables.

questions.stem: Which ECC Queue message contains the XML payload returned from the MID Server?
questions.explanation: The Input queue ECC message contains the XML payload returned from the MID Server. When a MID Server completes a probe execution, it sends the results back to the ServiceNow instance via the ECC Queue with Queue='Input' and State='Ready'. The Output queue contains outbound probe requests, not returned data.

questions.stem: Which of the following executes the osquery commands on agents to gather attribute details from a CI?
questions.explanation: Check Definitions in the Agent Client Collector (ACC) framework execute the osquery commands on agents to gather attribute details from a CI. A check definition contains the specific osquery SQL statements that query the endpoint for hardware, software, and configuration data. Policies schedule when checks run, and the Agent Collector is the runtime framework.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of Discovery Range Sets?

options.text: Range Sets are the only way to have more than one IP Range defined within a Discovery Schedule.
Range Sets show the number of IPs in a subnet.
All the necessary Range Sets are installed in the base installation of Discovery.
Range Sets provide flexibility in management and identification of known networks for simplicity of administration.

questions.explanation: The advantage of Discovery Range Sets is that they provide flexibility in management and identification of known networks for simplicity of administration. Range sets allow grouping related IP ranges together for reuse across multiple Discovery Schedules. They are not the only way to define multiple ranges, and not all needed ranges come pre-installed.

questions.stem: From Pattern Designer, which horizontal pattern type is the image below showing?
questions.explanation: Based on the image context from Pattern Designer, the horizontal pattern type shown is Infrastructure. Infrastructure patterns discover operating systems, hardware, and network infrastructure. The image likely shows pattern steps with operations typical of infrastructure discovery such as WMI queries, SSH commands, or SNMP queries.

questions.stem: Which of the following fields are editable from a Merge Table pattern operation? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: From a Merge Table pattern operation, the editable fields are Target Table (the output table where merged data goes), Second Table (the second source table), and First Table (the first source table). These three fields define the merge operation's inputs and output. Primary Table is not the standard field name used in Merge Table operations.

questions.stem: While discovering a new SNMP network device, which choice could cause the error “Active, couldn’t classify” to occur on a Discovery Status?

options.text: A firewall blocking the communication between the MID Server and the target device.
SNMP only behavior is not configured.
An SNMP Classification must be updated or created for the new device.

questions.explanation: The 'Active, couldn't classify' error on a Discovery Status for a new SNMP network device means the device was reached and responded (Active) but no matching SNMP Classification exists. An SNMP classification must be created or updated for the new device type. Firewall issues would prevent the Active status, and incorrect credentials would cause auth errors.

questions.stem: The deletion strategy is set to ‘Mark as absent’ for related Disk CIs discovered via the Linux Server pattern. If a related Disk CI is discovered during the Linux Server discovery and then the same related Disk CI is not found the next time the Linux Server is discovered, the following will happen:

options.text: The Disk Status CI (install_status) is set to Absent.
The Disk CI Operational Status (operational_status) is set to Non-Operational.
The Linux Server CI Operational Status (operational_status) is set to Non-Operational.
The Linux Server CI Status (install_status) is set to Absent.

questions.explanation: With deletion strategy set to 'Mark as absent', when a previously discovered Disk CI is not found during the next Linux Server discovery, the Disk CI's install_status is set to Absent. This marks the disk as no longer present without deleting the record. The Linux Server CI itself is not affected — only the missing related Disk CI is marked.

questions.stem: What would you see in the Discovery pattern log that you would not see in the ECC Queue?

options.text: Success or failure of the individual pattern steps
Payload of CI attributes and relationships

questions.explanation: The Discovery pattern log shows success or failure of individual pattern steps, which is not available in the ECC Queue. Pattern logs provide step-by-step execution details including which operations succeeded or failed. The ECC Queue only shows the overall probe/sensor communication payloads, not individual step results.

questions.stem: What do most Discovery properties start with?
questions.explanation: Most Discovery properties start with the prefix 'glide.discovery'. This is the standard namespace for Discovery-related system properties in ServiceNow. Examples include glide.discovery.debug, glide.discovery.ip_range, etc. The other prefixes (discovery.prop, disco.release, glide.itom) are not standard Discovery property prefixes.

questions.stem: What is the default thread count for a MID Server?
questions.explanation: The default thread count for a MID Server is 25. This determines how many concurrent operations the MID Server can process simultaneously. Increasing the thread count allows more parallel discovery operations but requires additional memory. The thread count can be adjusted in the MID Server configuration.

questions.stem: What is the recommended method for excluding specific software from discovery on Windows and Unix Servers?
questions.explanation: The recommended method for excluding specific software from discovery on Windows and Unix Servers is through the Configuration Console. This centralized configuration interface allows administrators to define software exclusion rules without modifying default patterns or probes. Pattern and probe modifications are not recommended as they can break during upgrades.

questions.stem: Which of the choices best describes a tabular variable in a discovery pattern?

options.text: Each cell is a CI attribute
Each cell is a scalar variable

questions.explanation: A tabular variable in a discovery pattern is best described as having each cell as a scalar variable. A tabular variable is essentially a table/matrix where each row represents a record and each cell contains a single scalar value. This allows patterns to process multi-row query results where individual cells can be referenced independently.

questions.stem: When configuring the MID Server Service Settings, which of the following is not a valid MID Server name?
questions.explanation: The MID Server name 'mid.server1' is not valid because MID Server names cannot contain periods (dots). Valid names use alphanumeric characters and underscores. Names like my_mid_server1, mid_server1, and midserver1 are all valid since they use only letters, numbers, and underscores.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not used in a horizontal discovery pattern?
questions.explanation: A Connectivity section is not used in a horizontal discovery pattern. Horizontal patterns use Variables, Operations (within steps), Identification sections (for CI identification), and Connection sections (for establishing relationships). 'Connectivity section' is not a standard component of horizontal patterns.

questions.stem: During the Port Scan phase what could the Warning level error “No results returned from probe.” mean?

options.text: Logical or physical firewall preventing connectivity

questions.explanation: During the Port Scan phase, the Warning level error 'No results returned from probe' typically means a logical or physical firewall is preventing connectivity between the MID Server and the target. The Shazzam probe cannot reach the target to scan ports. Process classifier issues, wrong credentials, and data source precedence are not relevant during port scanning.

questions.stem: Which of the choices are types of temporary variables in a discovery pattern? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two types of temporary variables in a discovery pattern are Tabular/Table (multi-row data structures from queries) and Scalar/List (single values or lists of values). These are the standard temporary variable types used within pattern steps for storing intermediate discovery data. SQL statements and Commands are operation types, not variable types.

questions.stem: What operation is shown in this image?
questions.explanation: Based on the image context, the operation shown is likely a Transform Table operation. Transform Table operations modify the structure or content of tabular data within a pattern, converting data from one format to another. Without seeing the exact image, this is the most common operation shown in exam exhibits.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the recommended permission level for credentials to discover Windows Servers?

options.text: A standard domain user with read access
A domain user with local administrator access
A user with root access across the domain
A domain administrator with sudo access

questions.explanation: The recommended permission level for discovering Windows Servers is a domain user with local administrator access. Local admin privileges are needed to query WMI, registry, and file system information. Standard domain users lack sufficient access, root is a Linux concept, and domain administrator with sudo mixes Windows and Linux concepts unnecessarily granting excessive access.

questions.stem: Which of the following are contained in an extension section of a discovery pattern?
questions.explanation: An extension section in a discovery pattern contains Shared libraries. Shared libraries are reusable collections of pattern steps that can be referenced across multiple patterns, reducing duplication. Extension sections execute these shared libraries after the main identification process completes. Connection sections and identification sections are separate pattern components.

questions.stem: Which of the below choices are possible options under ACTION ON ALL in the Recommended Actions pane for an Automated Error Messages list within Discovery > Home? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Under ACTION ON ALL in the Recommended Actions pane for Automaton Error Messages, the available options include Ping IP Addresses (to verify connectivity to all error IPs) and Retry Discovery (to reattempt discovery for all failed devices). View instructions is informational, not an action, and Make Ranges is not a standard bulk action option.

questions.stem: For a Parse Variable operation, when using the Delimited Text parsing strategy, which options are available in a step? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When using the Delimited Text parsing strategy in a Parse Variable operation, the available options are Positions (specifying which position/field to extract after splitting) and Delimiters (defining the character(s) used to split the text). SNMP Browser is for SNMP operations, and Merge Criteria is for Merge Table operations, not Parse Variable.

questions.stem: How do you create relationships between CIs in a horizontal pattern?

options.text: Relationships are created automatically for each successful connection section.
By using the Create Connections operation.
By using the Create Relation/Reference operation.
Relationships cannot be created via patterns.

questions.explanation: Relationships between CIs in a horizontal pattern are created using the Create Relation/Reference operation. This operation explicitly defines the relationship type and target CI. Relationships are not automatically created from connection sections (connections are about protocol connectivity). The Create Connections operation establishes network connectivity, not CI relationships.

questions.stem: CI identifiers can be viewed under which of the following?
questions.explanation: CI identifiers can be viewed under the CI Class Manager. This tool provides a centralized view of identification rules, including which attributes are used to uniquely identify CIs of each class. The Discovery Dashboard, Process Handlers, and individual CI records do not provide a comprehensive view of CI identification rules.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes what may also be required when increasing the max number of threads for a MID Server?

options.text: updating the acl rules for the CMDB tables in ServiceNow
increase the amount of disk space on the MID Server host
increasing the memory allocated to the MID Server app.
increase the MID Server max payload size

questions.explanation: When increasing the maximum number of threads for a MID Server, you must also increase the memory allocated to the MID Server application. More concurrent threads consume more memory for processing probes and handling data. Insufficient memory with increased threads causes performance degradation or crashes. ACL rules, disk space, and payload size are separate concerns.

questions.stem: Which part of Agent Client Collector must be configured to run osquery commands on a CI?
questions.explanation: ACC Checks must be configured to run osquery commands on a CI. A Check defines the specific osquery SQL statements that query the endpoint for system data. Checks are assigned to CIs through Policies. The ACC Websocket Endpoint handles communication, and Credential-less Discovery and Infrastructure Patterns are separate Discovery features.

questions.stem: Which selections are necessary to trigger a custom pattern? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: To trigger a custom pattern, you must select a CI Type (defining which CMDB class the pattern discovers) and a CI Entry Point (defining how the pattern is triggered — TCP port, SNMP, etc.). These two selections determine when and for what device types the custom pattern executes. Asset Records, CI Classification, and Process Handlers are not pattern trigger requirements.

questions.stem: What are three ways of extending Discovery?
questions.explanation: The three ways of extending Discovery are Classifiers (for identifying and categorizing new device types), Probes and Sensors (for collecting custom data via the ECC Queue), and Discovery Patterns (for defining custom discovery logic in Pattern Designer). This matches the standard Discovery extension framework. Fingerprinting and Flow Designer are not primary extension methods.

questions.stem: What are the main KPIs for CMDB Health scorecard? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three main KPIs for the CMDB Health scorecard are Completeness (how thoroughly CI records are populated), Compliance (whether CIs meet relationship and attribute requirements), and Correctness (accuracy of CI data including duplicate and stale detection). Duplicates and Staleness are sub-metrics within Correctness, not standalone KPIs.

questions.stem: As a first step in horizontal discovery, where is the Shazzam probe input placed in a request?
questions.explanation: As the first step in horizontal discovery, the Shazzam probe input is placed in a request on the ECC Queue. The ECC Queue is the communication mechanism between the ServiceNow instance and MID Servers. The Shazzam probe request is written to the Output queue, and the MID Server picks it up for execution.
